cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training
Demonstrated commitment to creating a community that fosters equality of experience and opportunity and ensures that students, faculty, and staff of all backgrounds feel safe, welcome, and included.

The Deputy Chief Administrative Officer is a critical member of the UC Berkeley Haas administrative team supporting the work of senior leadership and the dean. Reporting directly to the Senior Vice Dean and Chief Strategy and Operating Officer, this position participates in high-level decision-making and the consultative development and implementation of business school strategy, particularly regarding organizational development, performance management, and training. The Deputy Chief Administrative Officer serves as a subject-matter expert in specific areas, owns a distinct portfolio of responsibilities, and acts as a thought partner and project manager on matters with school-wide implications.
Support senior leadership to enact policy and administrative change, developing and implementing strategies for change management to remove barriers to goal achievement and achieve strategic success.

Leads assessment/gap analysis planning and organizational development efforts, including assessing training needs and translating them to targeted training plans, facilitating workshops, building supervisory training models on delegation, assessment, feedback, and holding teams accountable, developing learning materials and evaluation metrics, and partnering with managers to align development initiatives with strategic goals, culture metrics, and succession planning.

Works with managers to build staff capability and lead change adoption, partnering with leaders at all levels to plan and implement change initiatives, ensure clear communication, role clarity, and sustained performance.

Consults and advises senior administrators on a variety of complex and sensitive matters. Collaborates closely with the Haas HR staff. Provides analysis on a broad range of managerial and operational issues.
Leads projects that support new Haas endeavors, including research, collaboration, analysis, and communication about operational and strategic elements of the work.

Supervises direct reports from the Dean's Office administrative staff and the faculty support unit. Hires, trains, coaches, manages, and evaluates direct reports in these areas. Proactively anticipates issues and resolves conflicts within these areas. Works with the Senior Vice Dean/CSOO to address more complex matters.
Participates in the creation, maintenance, and reporting of operational and budget processes, academic and/or staff FTE, finance, human resources, and space planning.

Professional Learning and growth: Actively contributes to a team environment that fosters and promotes a culture of belonging for all, within the unit and at Haas. Exemplifies Haas' four Defining Leadership Principles: 1) Question the Status Quo; 2) Confidence Without Attitude; 4) Students Always; and 4) Beyond Yourself. Completes required training on time and engages in opportunities for learning pertinent to the position or at the suggestion of the supervisor
Solid knowledge of organizational processes, protocols, and procedures with a focus on budget and personnel management within labor contract(s) and personnel policy.
Solid knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs.
Solid interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and counseling to effectively motivate others.
Solid skills to quickly evaluate complex issues and identify resolutions.
Strong ability to build and maintain relationships with a broad range of staff and faculty.
Advanced skills in short- and long-term planning, program and project management, facilitation, and collaboration.
Demonstrated skills in employee supervision and HR administration.
Sound strategic thinking and consulting skills in guiding the department toward workable strategies and solutions.
Strong ability to focus on priorities, strategies, and vision while maintaining discretion and full confidentiality.
